title: Testing with pytest and the test client

videos.script: Every lesson so far checked agenda by hand. Curl, a script, a look at the rows. That finds a problem once. {{title}} A test finds it every time the code changes, which is when problems arrive. {{why}} pytest-django makes a database for the run, and wraps every test in a transaction it never commits. Each test starts clean. {{db}} The test client sends a request through all of Django, except the network. One test counts queries. Add one harmless-looking line to a template, and one query becomes three. {{queries}} Lesson 12's doors become a table, and each row a test of its own. {{doors}} Celery tasks need no Redis in a test. One test checks the task is queued after the commit. Another checks it sends one e-mail, however often it runs. {{tasks}} FastAPI gets the same doors, on a database of its own. Then you forget a guard on purpose. Three doors fail, by name, before the change reaches anyone.
